summary: Sunderland City Council runs the city-centre car parks itself (surface car parks, the St Mary's and Sunniside multi-storeys, the new Riverside multi-storey at Farringdon Row and the Station Car Park on Holmeside). A statutory notice published on 8 May 2026 said charges would rise from 1 June 2026, mostly by 20p an hour in the surface car parks, with Sunday and bank holiday rates going from 3.00 to 3.50 pounds. Policy is built around the Riverside Sunderland regeneration: the 600-plus-space Riverside multi-storey opened in June 2023 on the edge of the centre, the council put 2 million pounds into upgrading St Mary's and Sunniside in 2025, and paid parking began at the Stadium of Light car parks in August 2025 (free under 2 hours). The council's own car-parks, residents' parking, EV and cabinet pages, and the Echo, BBC and Chronicle sites, were blocked by bot protection, so residents' schemes, Metro park-and-ride tariffs and any formal parking strategy could not be sourced; only a 2013 static car-park dataset and a quarterly park-and-ride occupancy statement were found for data provision.

items.text: A statutory notice published in the Sunderland Echo on 8 May 2026 said Sunderland City Council would vary parking charges from 1 June 2026. For the surface car parks the hourly rate rises by 20p (for example Boughton Street from 1.40 to 1.60 pounds, Charles Street from 1.10 to 1.30, Gorse Road from 0.90 to 1.10, Nile Street from 1.30 to 1.50), the all-day rate rises from 5.00 to 5.50 pounds, and the Sunday and bank holiday daily rate rises from 3.00 to 3.50 pounds. The page was read on 21 October 2026 and does not itself show that the changes took effect.
items.source_title: Notice of Variation of Parking Charges, Sunderland (page 1 of 2), Public Notice Portal / Sunderland Echo

items.text: The same notice lists Station Car Park (access via Holmeside, listed with the figure 194, apparently its bay count) rising from 1.50 to 1.70 pounds per hour and from 7.00 to 7.50 pounds per day, with Monday to Friday 3pm to midnight staying free. Sheepfolds car park and nearby on-street bays go from 50p to 70p per hour, and the St Peters Metro Station car park (paid parking under a 2025 order) from 60p to 80p per hour with the 3.50 pound daily rate unchanged.
items.source_title: Notice of Variation of Parking Charges, Sunderland (page 1 of 2), Public Notice Portal / Sunderland Echo

items.text: The notice also covers on-street pay bays in the city centre, which would move for example from 1.10 pounds per 30 minutes to 1.30 pounds per hour (Bridge Street, Foyle Street, Frederick Street), and pay-by-phone bays at Ashbrooke (Tunstall Terrace) from 90p to 1.10 pounds per hour. The two pages read do not list the St Mary's, Sunniside or Riverside multi-storey car parks.
items.source_title: Notice of Variation of Parking Charges, Sunderland (page 2 of 2), Public Notice Portal / Sunderland Echo

items.text: Sunderland City Council announced that its new multi-storey car park at Farringdon Row (Riverside Sunderland), with more than 600 spaces, was fully operational after a temporary opening for two concerts. It is cashless, runs outside normal working hours to support the evening economy, and works through pre-paid permits and paid parking.
items.source_title: Riverside car park opens doors (Sunderland City Council news, mysunderland.co.uk)

items.text: The council said the Riverside car park should reduce pressure on St Mary's multi-storey, and that its position on the edge of the centre, linked by the Strategic Transport Corridor, would cut congestion in the heart of the city. Consolidating parking in one large facility was meant to help achieve pedestrian priority within Riverside Sunderland.
items.source_title: Riverside car park opens doors (Sunderland City Council news, mysunderland.co.uk)

items.text: When the contractor was appointed for the Farringdon Row car park (then described as 650 spaces, with an initial 15 percent electric-vehicle spaces), the council leader said the aim was to position modern car parking at the edge of the city so people drive to Sunderland, not through it. The car park was to replace ageing car parks including the Civic Centre site.
items.source_title: Contractor appointed for new city centre car park (North East Times Magazine)

items.text: In May 2025 the council approved a programme of about 2 million pounds for maintenance and upgrades at its St Mary's and Sunniside multi-storey car parks (facades, solar panels, lighting and CCTV, public wi-fi, signage, cycle storage). A contractor was still to be appointed; the page does not say when the works start or finish.
items.source_title: City centre car parks set for major upgrade (Sunderland Business Partnership, republishing the council announcement)

items.text: The Riverside Sunderland masterplan aims to double the city-centre resident population from 2,500 to 5,000, with 133 homes planned on the former Vaux plot and 165 homes by Placefirst on Farringdon Row reported as about to start. This adds to expected parking demand around the Riverside car park, although the article does not mention parking.
items.source_title: Igloo to start on site at Riverside Sunderland (Place North East)

items.text: Paid parking was announced for the Stadium of Light car parks from 26 August 2025: free under 2 hours, 4 pounds for 2 to 4 hours, 8 pounds for 4 to 8 hours, 10 pounds for 24 hours, 30 pounds for a monthly season ticket, paid via the Evology app. Tariffs do not apply on Sunderland AFC men's first-team matchdays; the notice was published by a school based at the stadium, not by the council or the club.
items.source_title: Parking charges to be introduced to Stadium of Light car parks (Beacon of Light School)

items.text: A University of Sunderland student news site reported that the new Stadium of Light charges left commuters and students without a free alternative close to the city centre, quoting two regular users. It is a small set of interviews, not a survey.
items.source_title: Sunderland locals frustrated as Stadium of Light introduce parking charges (SportsByte, University of Sunderland)

items.text: Planning permission was granted in October 2022 for a multi-storey car park on Holmeside near the rebuilt railway station, with 404 spaces including 92 EV charging bays and cycle storage, part-funded by the Transforming Cities Fund. This page does not show whether that scheme was built as approved; the May 2026 tariff notice lists a Station Car Park on Holmeside with 194 bays.
items.source_title: Plans Approved for New Multi-Storey Car Park in Sunderland (GSSArchitecture)

items.text: Four 7kW fast chargers (charging up to eight vehicles at once) were reported as installed at St Mary's car park in the city centre, funded by a 600,000 pound North East LEP grant and supplied by SWARCO. This is a 2022 fact and current charger numbers were not confirmed.
items.source_title: New fast electric vehicle charging points unveiled in central Sunderland (Greenfleet)

items.text: The council's open dataset 'Sunderland Car Parks' on data.gov.uk lists 48 public car parks (surface, on-street, charged and multi-storey) with space counts, but was last updated in August 2013. The page was read on 21 October 2026 and shows no live occupancy feed.

The Tyne and Wear UTMC unit says it provides average occupancy for each Metro park-and-ride car park quarterly, for comparing sites and periods. The page was last updated in April 2022 and contains no figures in the text read on 21 October 2026.
items.source_title: Park and ride occupancy (North East Evidence Hub)

gaps: sunderland.gov.uk, icm.sunderland.gov.uk and mysunderland.co.uk (car-parks tariff page, parking charter, Holmeside/Station Car Park pages, EV charging pages, residents' Community Parking Management Schemes such as Seaburn Metro/Newcastle Road, cabinet and committee papers) returned a bot-protection challenge (403 'Just a moment'); not opened. The one mysunderland.co.uk article cited was read before the challenge appeared.

sunderlandecho.com articles (the 2024 Free after 3 and 10p changes, a September 2026 piece on the new Bonner's Field/St Peter's charge, RingGo fees, February 2026 proposals) were blocked or only seen as search snippets; not used. BBC and Chronicle Live were not reachable by the search tool and no pages were opened.
No formal Sunderland Parking Strategy, Keel Square parking decision, Sunniside Social parking detail or Vaux site car-park plan was found in readable sources.

Metro park-and-ride (Nexus/Travel North East) pages and the PATROL parking annual reports for Sunderland returned 404 or were unreachable; no current Metro park-and-ride tariff or capacity could be sourced.
Current EV charging provision in council car parks and the 2026 on-street EV hub and charge-point-operator decisions were only seen in search snippets; not used.

The January 2024 tariff change (about 10p an hour at 1,500-plus spaces; Free after 3 ended at multi-storey car parks) and the 2025 St Peters Metro order notices could not be opened (public notice pages 404); the May 2026 notice is the only tariff source read.
Whether the 1 June 2026 charges are now in force, and what the St Mary's, Sunniside and Riverside multi-storey tariffs are, was not confirmed from an official current page.
